content: A bad workman always blames his tools.
meaning: This proverb is used when someone blames the quality of their equipment or other external factors when they perform a task poorly.
example: I don’t think the problem is with the software. It’s just that a bad workman always blames his tools.

content: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
meaning: This proverb means that it is better to have something that is certain than take a risk to get more, where you might lose everything.
example: I know you want a better job, but don’t quit your current job until you have another one. Remember, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

content: A chain is only as strong as its weakest link.
meaning: This proverb means that a group of people can only be as successful as the weakest member.
example: We need to make sure that everyone is well-trained. A chain is only as strong as its weakest link.

content: A fool and his money are soon parted.
meaning: This proverb means that foolish people spend money carelessly and soon become poor.
example: I can’t believe he spent all his money on that car. A fool and his money are soon parted.

content: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
meaning: This proverb means that a friend who helps you when you really need help is a true friend.
example: I was in trouble, and she was there for me. A friend in need is a friend indeed.

content: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
meaning: This proverb means that every long journey starts with one small step.
example: I know it seems like a big project, but remember, a journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

content: A leopard cannot change its spots.
meaning: This proverb means that people cannot change their basic nature.
example: I know you think he’s changed, but remember, a leopard cannot change its spots.

content: A picture is worth a thousand words.
meaning: This proverb means that a picture can convey a complex idea more effectively than words.
example: I could try to describe it, but a picture is worth a thousand words.

content: A watched pot never boils.
meaning: This proverb means that time seems to pass more slowly when you are waiting for something to happen.
example: I know you’re excited, but a watched pot never boils.

content: Actions speak louder than words.
meaning: This proverb means that what people do is more important than what they say.
example: I know he said he would help, but remember, actions speak louder

content: All good things must come to an end.
meaning: This proverb means that nothing good can last forever.
example: I know you’re sad, but remember, all good things must come to an end.

content: All is fair in love and war.
meaning: This proverb means that in love and war, anything is acceptable.
example: I know you think it’s unfair, but remember, all is fair in love and war.

content: All that glitters is not gold.
meaning: This proverb means that not everything that looks precious or true turns out to be so.
example: I know it looks good, but remember, all that glitters is not gold.

content: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.
meaning: This proverb means that eating an apple every day can help to keep you healthy.
example: you may not like fruits but they keep you healthy, remember, an apple a day keeps the doctor away.

content: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.
meaning: This proverb means that it is better to try to avoid problems in the first place, rather than trying to fix them once they arise.
example: I know it seems like a lot of work, but remember, an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.

content: As you sow, so shall you reap.
meaning: This proverb means that the consequences of your actions will come back to you.
example: I know you think you can get away with it, but remember, as you sow, so shall you reap.

content: Beggars can't be choosers.
meaning: This proverb means that people who are in need must accept whatever help they are offered.
example: I know it’s not perfect, but remember, beggars can’t be choosers.

content: Better late than never.
meaning: This proverb means that it is better to do something late than to never do it at all.
example: I know it’s late, but remember, better late than never.

content: Absence makes heart grow fonder.
meaning: This proverb means that when people are apart, their love grows stronger.
example: When I was with him, he always fought with me, but now he cries for me on phone. I think distance made his heart grow fonder.

content: A cat has nine lives.
meaning: This proverb means that cats are able to survive accidents that would kill most animals.
example: I haven’t seen him in months, but I wouldn’t really worry about him. Everyone knows a cat has nine lives.

content: A diamond with a flaw is better than a common stone that is perfect.
meaning: A rare, precious opportunity that comes with some problems is better than a regular opportunity that seems to be perfect.
example: I would advise you to work in a market that is growing fast than in a mature market. The former has its own problems, but that’s where you grow fast in your career. A diamond with a flaw is better than a common stone that is perfect.

content: A drowning man will clutch a straw.
meaning: When someone is in a difficult situation, s/he will take any available opportunity to come out of it.
example: After trying all reliable medicines, he is now visiting quacks to get a cure for his baldness. A drowning man will clutch a straw.

content: After victory, tighten your helmet chord.
meaning: This proverb means that after achieving success, one should be more careful.
example: I know you have won the first round, but remember, after victory, tighten your helmet chord.

content: A good listener is a silent flatterer.
meaning: people have an innate desire to be listened, but only few are good listeners. So, if you listen to someone attentively, you’ll flatter them.

content: A goose quill is more dangerous than a lion’s claw.
meaning: Foul, inconsiderate words can cause more pain than a physical attack.

content: A happy heart is better than a full purse.
meaning: This proverb means that happiness is more important than wealth.

content: All is well that ends well.
meaning: As long as the outcome is good, problems on the way don’t matter.

content: All lay loads on a willing horse.
meaning: People take advantage of those who are willing to help.

content: All roads lead to Rome.
meaning: There are many different ways to reach the same goal.

content: Among the blind, one-eyed man is king.
meaning: An incapable person can gain powerful position if others in the fray are even more incapable.

content: An army of sheep led by a lion would defeat an army of lions led by a sheep
meaning: A strong army (lions) led by a weak leader (sheep) can lose to a weak army (sheep) led by a strong leader (lion)

content: An empty vessel makes much noise
meaning: Fools and persons with shallow knowledge often talk a lot

content: An hour in the morning is worth two in the evening
meaning: People are generally more productive in the morning: first, they're fresh after night's sleep; second, there are fewer distractions in the morning

content: An idle brain is devil's workshop
meaning: If you've nothing to do, you'll likely think of mischief

content: An ounce of protection is worth a pound of cure
meaning: A little precaution before a crisis is better than lot of firefighting afterwards

content: A picture is worth a thousand words
meaning: It is easier to explain something through a picture than through words

content: A rolling stone gathers no moss
meaning: A person who is constantly changing his job and relationships won't have depth in any of them and would be unfulfilled

content: A ship in the harbor is safe, but that's not what a ship is for
meaning: Get out of your comfort zone to grow and fulfill your potential

content: Ask no questions and hear no lies
meaning: Don't ask questions which people can't or don't want to answer. If you ask such questions, you'll hear only lies

content: A stitch in time saves nine
meaning: It's better to deal with problems immediately than wait, by when they worsen and become much bigger

content: A thing begun is half done
meaning: A good beginning makes it easier to accomplish rest of the project

content: A tree is known by its fruit
meaning: Like a tree is known by the fruit it bears, people are known by their character and actions (and not by their appearance)

content: Barking dogs seldom bite
meaning: People who appear threatening rarely do harm

content: Beauty is in the eye of beholder
meaning: What may seem beautiful to one person may not seem to another

content: Beauty is only skin deep
meaning: A person's character, intellect, and other inner qualities are more important than his/her physical appearance

content: Begin to weave and God will give the thread
meaning: When taking up a task that has no playbook to follow, we plan a lot and think a lot but don't act. In such pursuits, you can't foresee everything in advance and lot of assumptions will come to naught. What's required is action. Plan, but act. Often, new paths open as you move forward

content: Be slow in choosing, but slower in changing
meaning: Choose things or people after diligence, but once you choose, stick for long

content: Best things in life are free
meaning: Most valuable things are often free

content: Better late than never
meaning: It is better to get something (you desire) late than get it never

content: Better to be poor and healthy than rich and sick
meaning: Health is more important than money

content: Birds of a feather flock together
meaning: People with similar nature seek out each other's company

content: Blood is thicker than water
meaning: Relationships with family is stronger than other relationships

content: Clothes do not make a man
meaning: A person's character can't be judged by his/her clothing and outward appearance

content: Cowards die many times before their death
meaning: Cowards suffer the feared effects of death many times in their lives

content: Cross the stream where it is shallowest
meaning: Do things in the easiest possible way

content: Curiosity killed the cat
meaning: Enquiring into others' work can be dangerous. One should mind own business

content: Curses, like chickens, come home to roost
meaning: The consequence of wrongdoings always catches up with the wrongdoer

content: Different strokes for different folks
meaning: Different people have different needs and wants, and we should be respectful to them

content: Discretion is the better part of valor
meaning: It is wise to be careful and not show unnecessary bravery

content: Do as you would be done by
meaning: Treat others like the way you would like to be treated. Some people, for example, ingratiate themselves with the powerful but treat less powerful with contempt. Don't be like them

content: Doctors make the worst patients
meaning: It's difficult to advice a person on a matter in which he is an expert. This is because he thinks that he already knows the best about what to do

content: Don't bite the hand that feeds you
meaning: Don't act badly toward the person who has helped you or from whom you derive some benefits, for you may lose those benefits in future

content: Don't carry coals to Newcastle
meaning: In the past, Newcastle was known for its coal mines. Coal was mined here and taken to other parts of England. So, if you carry coal to Newcastle, you're doing unnecessary work

content: Don't cast pearls before swine
meaning: Don't offer something valuable to someone who doesn't value it

content: Don't count your chickens before they hatch
meaning: Don't make plans based on future events that may not happen

content: Don't cross the bridge till you come to it
meaning: Deal with a situation when it happens and not unnecessarily worry about it in advance

content: Don't empty the water jar until the rain falls
meaning: Don't quit something, say a job, before securing its replacement

content: Don't judge a book by its cover
meaning: Just like you can't form an opinion of a book just by looking at its cover, you can't form an opinion about someone (or something) from their outward appearance

content: Don't kill the goose that lays golden eggs
meaning: If you kill a goose that lays golden eggs, you destroy something that makes lot of money for you

content: Don't open a shop unless you know how to smile
meaning: It's difficult to attract customers without a pleasant persona

content: Don't put all your eggs in one basket
meaning: Don't put all your effort into a single course of action, venture, investment, goal, or the like, because if it doesn't work, you lose everything

content: Don't think there are no crocodiles because the water is calm
meaning: Everything calm and peaceful doesn't mean there are no dangers around

content: Don't throw the baby with the bathwater
meaning: Don't discard something valuable while getting rid of something worthless

content: Eagles don't catch flies
meaning: Eagles catch bigger prey than flies, don't they? Don't take trivial matters to senior leaders in your organization. You have to resolve them, not they

content: Early bird catches the worm
meaning: One who starts early on the work has higher chance of success

content: Empty bags can't stand upright
meaning: A poor or hungry person cannot discharge his duties well

content: Every cloud has a silver lining
meaning: Bad times will eventually give way to better times. (The presence of silver lining means that the sun is behind the cloud and will eventually emerge.)

content: Every dog has his day
meaning: Even the unluckiest or the most unfortunate will taste success at some point

content: Every horse thinks its own pack is heaviest
meaning: We think that we work the hardest. This is also called responsibility bias: People tend to overvalue their own contributions and undervalue contributions of others

content: Every tub must stand on its own bottom
meaning: We can't hide incompetency behind teamwork. Everyone has to justify their expense

content: Fall seven times; stand up eight
meaning: Be resilient and try despite failures. That's how you succeed

content: Familiarity breeds contempt
meaning: If you know a situation, person, or thing well, you start taking them for granted and stop respecting them

content: Faults are thick where love is thin
meaning: If the love is shallow, people will find faults in each other

content: Fine feathers make fine birds
meaning: Like birds with colorful feathers look attractive, people in fine clothes look appealing. However, don't get swayed by external appearance when making friends

content: Flattery, like perfume, should be smelled but not swallowed
meaning: Enjoy the flattery you receive, but don't believe it because people often flatter to meet their own selfish interests

content: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread
meaning: Fools or inexperienced persons get involved in situations or pursue goals without much thought. In contrast, wise think through such situations or goals

content: Fortune favors the brave
meaning: If you carry out your plans boldly, luck is more likely to favor you

content: For want of a nail the shoe is lost, for want of a shoe the horse is lost, for want of a horse the rider is lost
meaning: An insignificant nail resulted in the loss of the rider. Small things can have huge implications. So, don't ignore nuances and minute details. They're the ones that stand people out

content: Get out while the going (getting) is good
meaning: Get out of a situation while it's still easy to leave on good terms

content: God helps those who help themselves
meaning: God helps those who make sincere effort

content: Good bargains empty the purse
meaning: Good bargains can be tempting and entice people into buying more than required, most of which can even go unused

content: Good swimmers are often drowned
meaning: Overconfidence can doom even the competent

content: Good things come to those who wait
meaning: Patience is often rewarded

content: Good wine needs no bush
meaning: A good product doesn't need promotion; it spreads through word of mouth

content: Grief divided is made lighter
meaning: If you share your grief, it'll get easier to bear

content: Half a loaf is better than none
meaning: We should thank for what we get even though it's less than what we had hoped for

content: Home is where the heart is
meaning: Don't you feel relieved on reaching home after you've been away for few days? No matter where you visit, you'll long to return to your home and family

content: Honesty is the best policy
meaning: It's always better to be truthful and honest, even if the opposite may get you short-term benefits

content: Hope for the best, but prepare for the worst
meaning: Be optimistic, but be prepared for a scenario where things can go wrong

content: If wishes were horses, beggars would ride
meaning: If things were to happen by just wishing them, even the poorest will have everything they want

content: If you are patient in a moment of anger, you will escape hundred days of sorrow
meaning: Actions and decisions taken in moments of anger aren't the best. They can bring great misery. Wait for your anger to pass and then act or decide

content: If you buy cheaply, you pay dearly
meaning: Something cheap will be of suspect quality and will trouble you later in the form of higher maintenance and/or poor performance

content: If you can't beat them, join them
meaning: If you can't beat your opponent, then work alongside them for mutual benefit

content: If you play with fire, you'll get burned
meaning: If you do something dangerous or adventurous, you may get harmed

content: If you want peace, prepare for war
meaning: If you utilize the peace time to get better at war, your adversaries will hesitate in waging a war on you, and hence the time of peace will stretch

content: If you want to go quickly, go alone. If you want to go far, go together
meaning: Working with others may be somewhat slow compared to solo work, but you'll need to collaborate if you want long-term success because you can't do everything yourself

content: Ignorance is bliss
meaning: If you don't know about something, you don't need to bother about it. In other words, if you're unaware of something, it won't cause you stress

content: Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery
meaning: Words of flattery may not be sincere. But action (imitation) is sincere. Who wouldn't be flattered if someone imitates them in some way?

content: It's better to be safe than sorry
meaning: It's better to be cautious than regret later

content: It's better to lose the battle and win the war
meaning: It's fine to lose small things if it helps you win the big pie

content: It is easy to find a thousand soldiers, but hard to find a good general
meaning: Leaders are not easy to find. Retain them at whatever price it takes if you've them

content: It's never too late to mend
meaning: It's never too late to change course or make amends for a past mistake. Don't let your ego come in between

content: It is part of a good shepherd to shear his flock, not to skin it
meaning: People shouldn't be subjected to discomfort beyond tolerance

content: It takes a village to raise a child
meaning: It takes an entire community to raise children in safe and nourishing environment

content: It takes two to make a quarrel
meaning: Without involvement of at least two persons, a quarrel won't happen. So, if one of the two persons decide, a quarrel won't happen

content: It takes two to tango
meaning: Where two parties are involved in a situation, fault usually lies with both if things go wrong. Rarely can one party be blamed entirely

content: Justice delayed is justice denied
meaning: In many countries, wheels of justice move so slow that sometimes it takes decades to pronounce a judgment. This causes suffering in terms of time and money wasted and the long wait for justice

content: Kind words will unlock an iron door
meaning: If you talk politely, people are more amenable to your suggestions and ask

content: Kings have long arms
meaning: Governments have far-reaching powers

content: Laughter is the best medicine
meaning: Laughter reduces stress and improves immunity, leading to better health

content: Learn to walk before you run
meaning: Learn basic skills first before venturing into complex things

content: Least said, soonest mended
meaning: When you fall out with someone, restrain yourself from using foul, upsetting language. Words can leave a lasting impression and make it difficult to reconcile

content: Lend your money and lose your friend
meaning: Lending money to a friend can lead to souring of friendship. If you ask to repay, he may feel offended, and if he fails to repay, you'll be offended

content: Let sleeping dogs lie
meaning: Don't talk about a bad situation people have forgotten and that could unnecessarily create problem in the present

content: Lightning never strikes twice in the same place
meaning: Misfortune does not occur twice in the same way to the same person

content: Like people, like priest
meaning: Quality of people is a good indicator of the quality of their leader. We expect our bureaucracy, politicians, and other leaders to be impeccable. But they don't descend from heavens. They come from the very people they represent, and hence their quality will be reflective of the quality of people

content: Long absent, soon forgotten
meaning: If you haven't met or spoken to a friend or relative in long time, he'll be forgotten. Such friendships eventually wither away or may just remain a distant acquaintance

content: Look before you leap
meaning: Consider all consequences before taking an action, especially when you can't retract

content: Love me, love my dog
meaning: If you love someone, then you should love them as they come with their qualities, shortcomings, friends, family, and so on

content: Make hay while the sun shines
meaning: Make the most of favorable conditions till they last

content: Make yourself all honey and the flies will devour you
meaning: If you're a yes-man and often talk sweet language to please others, people won't respect you

content: Money doesn't grow on trees
meaning: Spend money carefully because it's limited. You can't grow it on trees and replenish

content: Money talks
meaning: Money gives one power and influence

content: More die of food than famine
meaning: More people die because of excess indulgence in food and eating unhealthy than because of shortage of food

content: Murder will out
meaning: Secrets rarely remain secret. They'll eventually come out and be known to all

content: Necessity is the mother of invention
meaning: A need or problem forces people to come up with innovative solutions

content: Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today
meaning: Don't delay doing something if you can do it immediately

content: Never test the depth of water with both feet
meaning: If you're testing the depth of water with both feet down, you risk being drowned if the water turns out to be deep. But if you test with one foot, you can pull away. The proverb means that before going whole hog into something unknown, assess the risk well

content: Night brings counsel
meaning: If you have a difficult problem to solve or an important decision to make, a good night's sleep will work wonders

content: No gain without pain
meaning: To succeed in one's pursuits, it is necessary to work hard and sacrifice pleasures

content: No news is good news
meaning: If you don't receive any news about someone or something, it means that everything is fine and going normally

content: Oaks may fall when reeds stand the storm
meaning: Those who are flexible and relatively insignificant can survive a crisis that brings down powerful who are unable or unwilling to adapt

content: Once bitten twice shy
meaning: A person won't do something a second time because he/she had bad experience the first time

content: One man's junk is another man's treasure
meaning: What may seem to be junk to one person maybe valuable to another

content: Pen is mightier than sword
meaning: Thinking and writing have more influence on people and events than use of force

content: People who live in glass houses shouldn't throw stones at others
meaning: People who have some shortcomings shouldn't criticize others for having the same shortcomings

content: Persuasion is better than force
meaning: You can achieve better results through persuasion than through coercion

content: Politeness costs little but yields much
meaning: Speaking politely costs no more than speaking rudely, but it can yield much more by making friends

content: Practice makes perfect
meaning: Doing something over and over makes one better at it

content: Practice what you preach
meaning: Behave the way you encourage others to behave

content: Rich man's joke is always funny
meaning: People agree with and flatter rich people to be in good books with them

content: Rome wasn't built in a day
meaning: Important work takes time to complete

content: Shrouds have no pockets
meaning: We arrived in this world without anything, and we'll leave without anything

content: Silence is half consent
meaning: If you don't object to what someone says or does, you may be assumed to agree to some extent

content: Slow and steady wins the race
meaning: Slow and consistent work leads to better chance of success than quick work in spurts

content: Smooth seas do not make skillful sailors.
meaning: If you work only on regular projects, you won't be challenged and hence not become better at what you do.

content: Still water runs deep.
meaning: If a person doesn't speak much, it doesn't mean they lack depth or are uninteresting.

content: Strike while the iron is hot.
meaning: Take advantage of an opportunity before it extinguishes.

content: The course of true love never did run smooth.
meaning: True love goes through ups and downs.

content: The family that (eats) prays together stays together.
meaning: The family that gets together regularly to pray or eat is more close-knit than the family that doesn't.

content: The grass is greener on the other side of fence.
meaning: People are never satisfied with their own situation; they always think others have it better.

content: The harder you work, the luckier you get.
meaning: The harder you work, the more ideas and chances you may make for yourself.

content: The higher the monkey climbs the more he shows his tail.
meaning: The higher an incompetent person rises in an organization, the more his incompetence is exposed.

content: The highest branch is not the safest roost.
meaning: Those in the highest positions can be vulnerable as many aspire to replace them.

content: The longest way around is the shortest way home.
meaning: If you want to achieve the desired quality, work diligently and carefully and not cut corners.

content: The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.
meaning: If you deviate from the norm, you'll face resistance, even hostile reaction in extreme case.

content: The only free cheese is in the mousetrap.
meaning: There rarely are completely free offers; they come attached with hooks.

content: The proof of pudding is in eating.
meaning: You can only judge the quality of something after you have tried, used, or experienced it.

content: There are many paths to the top of the mountain, but the view is always the same.
meaning: We all want peace and happiness in life, and there are multiple ways of achieving this goal.

content: There are more ways than one to skin a cat.
meaning: There is more than one way to reach the same goal.

content: There is no time like the present.
meaning: The best time to do something is right now. So, act now.

content: There is truth in wine.
meaning: People when drunk speak truth, often unwittingly.

content: The road to hell is paved with good intentions.
meaning: Good intention doesn't matter if a person's actions lead to bad outcomes.

content: The squeaky wheel gets the grease.
meaning: People who complain the most are the ones who get attention or what they want.

content: The tongue is but three inches long, yet it can kill a man six feet tall.
meaning: We should avoid foul, inconsiderate language because it can leave lasting scars and dent relationships forever.

content: Time and tide wait for no man.
meaning: You've no control over passage of time; it'll keep slipping. So don't procrastinate, don't delay things.

content: To know the road ahead, ask those coming back.
meaning: Many take up a job or project they later hate, wasting precious years. This can be avoided if you ask few who've undertaken the same job or project about their experience.

content: Too many cooks spoil the broth.
meaning: When too many people work together on a project, the result is inferior.

content: Two heads are better than one.
meaning: Two persons have a better chance to solve a problem than one.

content: Two wrongs don't make a right.
meaning: You shouldn't harm a person who has harmed you, even if you think that person deserves it.

content: Restless feet may walk into a snake pit
meaning: When you have nothing good to do, you might land in trouble.

content: Two wives are like two pots of poison
meaning: Possessing more things means more threat.

content: Ears that do not listen to advice accompany the head when chopped off
meaning: A person who does not follow good advice will suffer.

content: A tree cannot stand without roots
meaning: Roots are the foundation of existence, which no one can ever take away.

content: You begin with the meal before the water is boiling
meaning: Someone too impatient.

content: Don't be afraid of the forest because it's dark
meaning: Don't give up on things when they appear hard.

content: Wherever a man goes to dwell, his character goes with him
meaning: A man's character defines him.

content: He who does not brush his teeth before breakfast complains about sour food
meaning: An unprepared person complains about the situation.

content: Even the best dancer on the stage must retire sometime
meaning: Nothing lasts forever.

content: If there is no enemy within, the enemy outside cannot harm
meaning: When there are no negative thoughts in your mind, others can not harm you.

content: If you heal a person's leg, do not be surprised if they run away
meaning: If you teach a skill to someone, they can use it against you.

content: A roaring lion kills no game
meaning: You won't get far if you sit around and talk about it.

content: When you befriend a chief, keep in mind that he sits on a rope
meaning: No matter how free we wish to live, the obligations of our roles constrain us.

content: Getting up early shortens the journey
meaning: Preparing for something beforehand makes the process easier.

content: A single bracelet does not jingle
meaning: The power of numbers is undeniable.

content: If you have pride, you will have no room for wisdom
meaning: Only one who is humble can attain wisdom.

content: Whoever seeks good fortune does it at the expense of peace
meaning: Chasing after money leads to a chaotic life.

content: Eat when the food is ready. Speak when the time is right
meaning: Do something when it is the right time.

content: He has twelve professions but thirteen mishaps
meaning: A person good at a number of things but not great at anything.

content: Smooth seas do not make skilful sailors
meaning: Comfortable situations don't hone your skills.

content: Sugarcane is sweetest at the joint
meaning: In the everyday world, what appears to be difficult to achieve is usually the greatest.

content: Coffee and love taste best when hot
meaning: You can enjoy some moments only at a particular time.

content: A woman is never old when it comes to the dance she knows
meaning: You are never too old to do something you are passionate about.

content: You learn how to cut down trees by cutting them down
meaning: You will only learn something by doing it.

content: Do not look where you fell but where you slipped
meaning: Don't focus on your failures; instead, consider what led to them.

content: If you close your eyes to facts, you will learn through accidents
meaning: Always seek the truth or get in trouble.

content: Don't set sail using someone else's star
meaning: Just because someone was successful following a path does not indicate you will be able to accomplish it.

content: The elephant does not limp when walking on thorns
meaning: Self-belief is necessary for success.

content: Gold should be sold to someone who understands its worth
meaning: Someone who understands the true worth of a valuable object achieves it.

content: The day the monkey dies, all the trees will get slippery
meaning: Fate turns in favour of a destined event.

content: Nobody is born wise
meaning: Wisdom comes from a relentless desire to learn and not from birth.

content: What you learn is what you'll take with you when you die
meaning: We leave the material things behind. Only our learning and deeds exist as our legacy.

content: Being lost is a great method to learn how to navigate
meaning: You will know to strive in life when you face problems.

content: Milk and honey have different colours. Yet they coexist peacefully in the same house.
meaning: Love each other and live peacefully despite the differences.

content: The axe fails to notice, but the tree remembers.
meaning: We can move on, but we cannot undo the damage.

content: Love like rain doesn’t decide the grass it rains on.
meaning: One should love without bias.

content: If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together.
meaning: Having a team takes time to get results. But teammates complement one another for their differences so that you can make it far.

content: It is better to be loved than to be feared.
meaning: Love is a powerful tool. It makes you a better person. Chose to receive love over fear.

content: All errors are amendable.
meaning: Making mistakes is human nature.

content: Don’t tell the man carrying you that he stinks if you don’t want to walk alone.
meaning: Value the person willing to help you. Don’t bother about their shortcomings.

content: Whoever adores the vase adores the contents as well.
meaning: If you love someone because of one aspect, you should like their other qualities.

content: Birds sing not because they have answers but because they have songs.
meaning: Every person we respect has a talent.

content: Once water spills, it cannot scoop back.
meaning: Some things can not change no matter what.

content: A person who sells eggs should not start a fight in the market.
meaning: Don’t trigger anything if you are vulnerable.

content: You’ll remember every drop once you start carrying your water.
meaning: You only know the value of something once it is gone.

content: Nobody takes medicine on an unwell person’s behalf.
meaning: Nobody will switch places with you in bad times.

content: Even if the cock does not crow, the sun will rise.
meaning: An inevitable event will happen no matter what.

content: Rain does not fall on just one roof.
meaning: Everyone faces difficulties at some point in their lives.

content: When the hyena falls into a bottomless pit, he does not shout for help.
meaning: No one helps a wicked person even in the worst situations.

content: Not everyone who chased the zebra caught it.
meaning: Trying doesn't guarantee success, but you can't succeed without trying.

content: Teeth do not see poverty.
meaning: People can find something to smile about even in difficult circumstances.

content: A child that does not cry will die in the carrier.
meaning: If you want something, you must ask for it.

content: You cannot shave someone in his absence.
meaning: If you do something wrong, people should tell you so you can learn and improve.

content: What an elder sees sitting down, a child cannot see it even if he climbs an iroko tree.
meaning: Wisdom comes with age.

content: A woman holds the knife at the sharp end.
meaning: This proverb acknowledges the challenges that women face.

content: Two rams cannot drink from the same bucket at the same time.
meaning: A Yoruba proverb that means people have different capabilities and preferences.
